sources.citation: Franklin, Karl J. & Joice Franklin. 1978. A Kewa dictionary, with supplementary grammatical and anthropological materials. Pacific Linguistics C-53. Canberra: ANU. Section 4.2 'Mendi vowels', pp. 82-90 (reprint of Franklin 1974, 'A diachronic note on Mendi vowels', Kivung 7/3: 167-77).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: First-hand on Mendi Proper (= East Angal [age]). Only incidental mentions: p.83 'lal has an allophone [ʌ] which occurs word finally in unstressed syllables' (reporting Rule & Rule 1960); p.85 'Mendi /a/.. In the final position of unstressed syllables it usually actualises as [ʌ]'; p.89 'undoubtedly linked to phonetic features of stress and tone'; p.89 §4.2.4 'the function of tone in Kewa and other languages of the family may sometimes carry the equivalent load of the extra vowel in Mendi'. No statement of where stress falls; no tone system stated for Mendi.

sources.citation: Tipton, Ruth A. 1982. Nembi procedural and narrative discourse. Pacific Linguistics B-82. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in (archive.org lending); also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number Philol69.57.3 no.82)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number Philol69.57.3 no.82
sources.note: On Nembi = Angal Enen [aoe] (anga1294), sister variety in the Mendi dialect chain. p.79: 'Nembi has two phonemic tones: high and low.. Tone, however, carries a low functional load in the language and is not.' No word-stress statement (the only 'stress' mention, p.10, is about English/Halliday).

sources.citation: Franklin, Karl J. 1975. Comments on Proto-Engan. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), PL C-38, 263-275.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative; notes tone disambiguates minimal pairs in present-day Engan languages; no stress statement. Bibliography names the Mendi primary sources: Rule 1965 (AnL 7/5), Rule & Rule 1960 'The Mendi Alphabet' (12pp duplicated), Schlatter 1962 Wala verb, unpublished wordlists.

sources.citation: Wurm, S.A. 1975. Eastern Central Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene, 461-526. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Survey. p.483 §2.7.2.2.5.5 West-Central Family (Enga, Huli, Ipili, Angal (Mendi), Kewa, Sau): 'characterised by the presence of palatalised consonant phonemes and the universal appearance of complex tonal systems'. Nothing on stress for Mendi; illustrative notes are for Enga only (two tonemes).

sources.citation: Schlatter, V. 1962. A preliminary sketch of the Wala verb. 14 pp. Mimeo (Apostolic Christian Mission); and Schlatter n.d. Wala orthography (cited Franklin 1978:83 fn.).
